texts.li: There's snow on the ground, real snow, the kind that packs. {A_nameDef} has come to the council with a petition signed by every child in the colony and two of the grown-ups: a snow day. No chores, no lessons, everyone outside.

{A_nameDef} woke the whole colony at dawn shouting that it had snowed. Now {A_nameDef} is standing in front of the council in three coats, asking for the day off for everyone, to build the biggest snowman the colony has ever seen.
[lowtech] Where {A_nameDef}'s parents came from, the first deep snow was a holiday: everyone out sliding on the hill, and a hot drink after. {A_nameDef} asks if it could be the same here.

li.label: A snow day for everyone
li.outcome: The whole colony went out in the snow: a snowman as tall as the door, a battle the children won, and sliding on the slope until dark. Nobody got any work done. Nobody minded.

outcomes.li: [quirk:WrongLaugh] {A_nameDef} hit the council's sternest member square in the face with a snowball and laughed so hard {A_pronoun} fell over. The council member threw one back. It went on until dark.
[lowtech] They slid down the hill on boards and sacks until the light went, and came in to something hot, and called it the snow day, and decided it should happen every year.

li.label: The children can play; the rest of us work
li.outcome: The children had their snow day, and the grown-ups watched from the windows, working. Several grown-ups found reasons to go outside more often than usual.

li.label: Snow means more work, not less
li.outcome: The council said snow means paths to clear and roofs to sweep. {A_nameDef} was given a shovel. {A_nameDef} built a very small snowman by the path, on {A_possessive} own, out of spite.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has marked out a race course round the fields with sticks and string, and wants the whole colony to come and watch the children run it one evening. There will be a prize. The prize is to be decided.

{A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun} is the fastest runner in the colony and wants it settled properly: a race, all the children, everyone watching, at midsummer. The other children have agreed, with conditions.
[lowtech] Back where {A_nameDef}'s family came from, the children ran the bounds of the fields every summer, so they'd know the land. {A_nameDef} would like to run them here, with everyone cheering.

li.label: Everyone comes out to cheer
li.outcome: The whole colony lined the course one long summer evening and cheered the children round it. {A_nameDef} came second, and argued about it until the stars were out. The prize was a honey cake, shared.

outcomes.li: [quirk:Volunteers] {A_nameDef} volunteered to run, to keep the course, to hand out the prize and to tidy up afterwards. {A_nameDef} came third, and was the happiest of anyone.

li.label: The children can race on their own
li.outcome: The children ran their race with only each other to cheer. {A_nameDef} won, apparently. Nobody else saw it.

li.label: No time for races this summer
li.outcome: The council said the summer is for work. {A_nameDef} took the string down from the course and coiled it very slowly, so everyone could see.

texts.li: The harvest is in, and {A_nameDef} has noticed how much is left lying in the stubble. {A_nameDef} asks if the children could glean the fields after the harvesters, and keep what they find for a feast of their own.

{A_nameDef} has a basket and a plan: every child in the colony walks the harvested fields, picks up what was missed, and the colony makes something with it that's the children's own. {A_nameDef} has asked the council.
[lowtech] In the old days, {A_nameDef} has been told, the gleanings belonged to the children and the poor, by right. {A_nameDef} would like that to be true here too.

li.label: The gleanings are the children's
li.outcome: The children walked the fields with baskets and came back with more than anyone expected. That evening the colony ate the gleanings together, and the children served, very seriously, and were thanked by everyone.

li.label: Glean, but it goes to the stores
li.outcome: The children gleaned the fields and everything went into the storeroom. {A_nameDef} carried in the last basket and put it down with a sigh that could be heard across the colony.

li.label: The animals can have the stubble
li.outcome: The council said the stubble was for the animals. {A_nameDef} picked one perfect ear of grain on the way back and kept it on {A_possessive} windowsill.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wants to plant a tree. Not just any tree: {A_possessive} tree, at the edge of the fields, with {A_possessive} name on a stone beside it. And then every child gets one. {A_nameDef} has thought this through.

{A_nameDef} found a sapling growing in a crack by the wall and wants to give it a proper home. The idea grew in the telling: every spring, every child plants a tree, and the colony grows a grove of them.

[lowtech] Where {A_nameDef}'s mother grew up, every child planted a tree in their first spring that could walk, and you could find anyone's age by the trunk. {A_nameDef} would like to start that here.

li.label: Every child plants a tree
li.outcome: The colony walked out to the edge of the fields one spring morning, and every child planted a sapling and put a stone beside it. {A_nameDef} watered {A_possessive} twice before breakfast and once after.

outcomes.li: [quirk:SoftSpot] {A_nameDef} planted {A_possessive} tree and then spent an hour building a little fence round it to keep the animals off, then left a pile of scraps outside the fence for them, as an apology.

li.label: the planting of the children's trees
Just {A_nameDef}'s tree, this year
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} planted {A_possessive} tree by the wall, alone, with a stone beside it. It's very small. {A_nameDef} says it'll be the tallest in the colony one day.

li.label: Trees take room from the crops
li.outcome: The council said the land is for crops. {A_nameDef} planted the sapling in a pot by {A_possessive} bed instead, and talks to it.
